description: #3830 — READ-command differential over the property-definition registry: `list_property_defs` and `get_property_def`. Both were waived as "registry, not projected block state" until a fixture could put the same registry on both stacks; `seed.property_defs` is that, and a fixture declaring it declares the WHOLE registry (the Rust seed clears migrations 0011/0014/0016/0035/0103's builtin declarations first, because the mock's map starts empty). The defs are seeded in NON-alphabetical order on purpose: `list_property_defs_inner` is `ORDER BY key ASC`, so the ordered comparison pins the sort rather than insertion order — the divergence this fixture found and fixed in the mock. Every token carries `value_type` and `options`, the whole of what a declaration says; `created_at` is a wall clock and is not comparable. The one op writes `status = todo` through `set_property`, which both stacks gate on the seeded select's `options`, so the declaration is load-bearing rather than decorative — and it is an OP rather than a `seed.properties` entry because the Rust seed writes those through `set_property_inner`, which appends an op_log entry the mock's direct seed write does not (no other fixture uses that section). NOT pinned: pagination (the mock serves every def in one page and ignores `cursor` / `limit`) and the builtin declarations themselves, which the mock has no copy of.
name: query_property_defs

queries.comment: `estimate` before `status`, though the seed declares `status` first: the listing is `ORDER BY key ASC`. The attributes pin the declaration itself — a select's `options` array and the `null` a non-select carries.
queries.name: property_defs_sorted_by_key

queries.comment: The PK lookup serves the same row the listing does, options and all. Paired with the next step, this is the present-vs-absent distinction.
queries.name: get_property_def_hit

queries.comment: The other half of the pair: `colour` was never declared, so the lookup misses and the command answers `None` rather than refusing or inventing an undeclared row. Empty on purpose — the previous step's hit is what makes the absence a real distinction instead of a vacuous one.
queries.name: get_property_def_miss
